questions.question_text: A university compares the average starting salaries of graduates from Engineering, Science, Commerce, and Arts using samples from each group. Which hypothesis pair is appropriate for a one-way ANOVA?

options.A: H₀: μ₁  μ₂  μ₃  μ₄; Hₐ: All means are equal
options.B: H₀: At least one population mean differs; Hₐ: All population means are equal
options.C: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ = μ₄; Hₐ: At least one population mean differs
options.D: H₀: μ₁ ≠ μ₂ ≠ μ₃ ≠ μ₄; Hₐ: All population means are equal

questions.explanation: In a one-way ANOVA, the null hypothesis ($H_0$) states that all group population means are equal ($H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \mu_3 = \mu_4$), while the alternative hypothesis ($H_a$) states that at least one population mean differs from the others.

questions.question_text: A researcher performs a one-way ANOVA to compare the average productivity of employees working under four different training programmes. The null hypothesis is rejected. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Every training programme has a significantly different mean productivity from every other programme.
options.B: The training programme with the largest sample mean is the best programme.
options.C: There is sufficient evidence that at least one programme has a different population mean productivity.
options.D: The sample means must all be different because the null hypothesis was rejected.

questions.explanation: Rejecting the null hypothesis in ANOVA indicates statistically significant evidence that at least one group's population mean productivity differs from the others, without specifying which or if all means differ.

questions.question_text: Why is the technique called Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) even though its objective is to compare population means?

options.A: Because ANOVA directly compares the variances of the populations instead of their means.
options.B: Because ANOVA assumes that all population variances are unequal before comparing means.
options.C: Because differences among population means are assessed by analysing the variation present within and between the sample groups.
options.D: Because the sample variances are always equal to the population means during the analysis.

questions.explanation: ANOVA evaluates population means by partitioning total variability into variability between group means and variability within sample groups, comparing these components using an F-test.

questions.question_text: Which of the following situations is most appropriate for applying a one-way ANOVA?

options.A: Determining whether the average income in a single city exceeds ₹8 lakh per year.
options.B: Comparing the proportion of customers preferring online shopping across four regions.
options.C: Estimating the average waiting time at a single hospital using a random sample.
options.D: Comparing the mean customer satisfaction scores across customers using four different mobile service providers.

questions.explanation: One-way ANOVA is designed to compare a continuous quantitative variable (satisfaction scores) across three or more categorical independent groups (four mobile service providers).

questions.question_text: A company wants to compare the average monthly sales generated by sales teams in four different regions. Which statistical method is most appropriate for testing whether the regional average sales are significantly different?

options.A: One-sample Z-test
options.B: One-Way ANOVA
options.C: Chi-Square Test
options.D: Simple Linear Regression

questions.explanation: One-Way ANOVA is the appropriate test when comparing the means of a single continuous outcome variable across three or more independent groups.

questions.question_text: A government evaluates the effectiveness of a welfare scheme across six states by comparing the average household income improvement in each state. In this study, the six states represent:

options.A: Six independent variables
options.B: Six response variables
options.C: Six observations
options.D: Six populations (factor levels/treatments)

questions.explanation: In ANOVA terminology, 'State' is the single factor (independent variable), and the six states correspond to the six factor levels, treatments, or populations being compared.

questions.question_text: The primary objective of one-way ANOVA is to determine whether:

options.A: Population variances are equal.
options.B: Sample means are identical.
options.C: Differences among sample means provide sufficient evidence that at least one population mean is different.
options.D: All observations follow a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: The main objective of a one-way ANOVA is to determine if observed sample mean differences provide statistically significant evidence that at least one population mean differs from the rest.

questions.question_text: Why is ANOVA preferred instead of repeatedly conducting multiple hypothesis tests when several populations are compared?

options.A: ANOVA requires fewer observations.
options.B: ANOVA evaluates all population means simultaneously using a single hypothesis test.
options.C: ANOVA compares population medians instead of means.
options.D: ANOVA ignores sampling variability.

questions.explanation: ANOVA tests all population means simultaneously in one test, controlling the family-wise Type I error rate that would inflate if multiple pairwise t-tests were conducted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following situations cannot be addressed directly using the one-way ANOVA discussed in the lecture?

options.A: Comparing average crop yields under four fertilizers.
options.B: Comparing average salaries across three academic disciplines.
options.C: Comparing average productivity across five manufacturing plants.
options.D: Estimating the average salary of employees in a single company.

questions.explanation: One-way ANOVA requires comparing two or more population groups. Estimating a single mean for one company is a one-sample inference problem and cannot be addressed with ANOVA.

questions.question_text: A student concludes that rejection of the null hypothesis implies that every population mean is different. Which statement best evaluates this conclusion?

options.A: It is correct because ANOVA compares all possible pairs.
options.B: It is correct only when there are three populations.
options.C: It is incorrect because rejection only indicates that at least one population mean differs.
options.D: It is incorrect because ANOVA tests variances rather than means.

questions.explanation: Rejection of the null hypothesis in ANOVA indicates that at least one group mean is significantly different from another, not that all group means are distinct from each other.

questions.question_text: In the simple linear regression model y = β0 + β1x + ε, how should the coefficient β1 be interpreted?

options.A: The predicted value of y when x equals zero
options.B: The change in the expected value of y for a one-unit increase in x
options.C: The proportion of variation in y explained by x
options.D: The correlation between x and y

questions.explanation: In a simple linear regression model, $\beta_1$ represents the slope coefficient, which measures the expected change in the dependent variable $y$ for every one-unit increase in the independent variable $x$.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes what “linearity” means in the context of a simple linear regression model?

options.A: The independent variable x must always take positive values.
options.B: The relationship between x and y must be a straight line with no exceptions.
options.C: The model must be linear in the parameters β0 and β1, not necessarily in the variables.
options.D: The error term ε must always be positive.

questions.explanation: In linear regression, 'linearity' specifically requires that the equation is linear in its parameters (coefficients $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$), even if the independent or dependent variables undergo non-linear transformations.

questions.question_text: The ordinary least squares (OLS) method chooses b0 and b1 to minimise which of the following quantities?

options.A: The total sum of squares (SSTotal)
options.B: The sum of squared residuals, Σ(yi − ŷi)².
options.C: The sum of the absolute values of the residuals.
options.D: The correlation coefficient between x and y.

questions.explanation: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) minimizes the sum of squared differences between observed values $y_i$ and predicted values $\hat{y}_i$, represented as $\sum (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$.

questions.question_text: The coefficient of determination, R², is calculated as:

options.A: SSR / SSTotal
options.B: SSE / SSTotal
options.C: SSTotal / SSR
options.D: 1 / SSE

questions.explanation: The coefficient of determination $R^2$ is defined as the ratio of Sum of Squares due to Regression (SSR) to Total Sum of Squares (SSTotal), representing the proportion of variance explained.

questions.question_text: In Hanumanthapa’s dataset, the regression of monthly credit card spend on annual income gave an R² of 0.65. What is the correct interpretation of this value?

options.A: 65% of the variation in annual income is explained by monthly spend.
options.B: 65% of the variation in monthly spend is explained by the estimated regression equation.
options.C: The correlation between income and spend is 0.65.
options.D: The regression equation is correct 65% of the time.

questions.explanation: $R^2 = 0.65$ indicates that 65% of the total variation in the response variable (monthly spend) is explained by its linear relationship with the predictor variable (annual income).

questions.question_text: If the coefficient b1 in an estimated regression equation is positive, how is the sample correlation coefficient r related to R²?

options.A: r = R²
options.B: r = the negative square root of R²
options.C: r = 1 − R²
options.D: r = the positive square root of R²

questions.explanation: In simple linear regression, $R^2 = r^2$. Since the slope coefficient $b_1$ is positive, the sample correlation $r$ must also be positive, making $r = +\sqrt{R^2}$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the standard assumptions about the error term ε in a simple linear regression model?

options.A: The error term has a mean of zero.
options.B: The variance of the error term is constant across all values of x (homoscedasticity).
options.C: The error terms are independent of one another.
options.D: The error term is perfectly correlated with the independent variable x.

questions.explanation: A key assumption of regression is that the error term $\varepsilon$ is independent of $x$ (zero correlation). Perfect correlation between the error term and $x$ violates standard OLS assumptions.

questions.question_text: In testing the significance of a simple linear regression relationship, the null hypothesis H0: β1 = 0 implies that:

options.A: The intercept of the regression line is zero.
options.B: There is no linear relationship between x and y in the population.
options.C: The regression equation provides a perfect fit.
options.D: The correlation coefficient must equal one.

questions.explanation: A slope $\beta_1 = 0$ means that changes in $x$ produce no change in the expected value of $y$, implying the absence of a linear relationship between $x$ and $y$ in the population.

questions.question_text: An ANOVA table for a simple linear regression produces an F-statistic with a p-value close to zero. What is the appropriate conclusion?

options.A: Reject the null hypothesis; there is sufficient evidence of a significant linear relationship.
options.B: Fail to reject the null hypothesis; the relationship is not significant.
options.C: The value of R² must be equal to zero.
options.D: The assumption of normality has been violated.

questions.explanation: A $p$-value close to zero (typically $< 0.05$) provides strong evidence to reject $H_0: \beta_1 = 0$, confirming that the linear relationship between $x$ and $y$ is statistically significant.

questions.question_text: For a regression model with normally distributed errors, standardised residuals are expected to lie within which range approximately 95% of the time?

options.D: 0 to +1

questions.explanation: Standardized residuals follow a standard normal distribution $N(0,1)$. By the empirical rule, approximately 95% of the values fall within two standard deviations of the mean ($-2$ to $+2$).

questions.question_text: A multiple linear regression model for monthly credit-card spending is estimated as: ŷ = 355.68 + 71.16x₁ + 339.9x₂ where x₁ is annual household income (₹ lakh) and x₂ is household size.

options.A: A ₹1 lakh increase in annual income causes monthly spending to increase by ₹71.16, irrespective of household size.
options.B: A ₹1 lakh increase in annual income is associated with an estimated ₹71.16 increase in monthly spending, holding household size constant.
options.C: A one-unit increase in household size is associated with an estimated ₹71.16 increase in monthly spending, holding income constant.
options.D: Households with ₹1 lakh higher income spend ₹71.16 more per month on average, without considering other variables.

questions.explanation: In multiple linear regression, the slope coefficient for an independent variable represents the estimated change in the dependent variable for a one-unit increase in that variable, holding all other independent variables constant (ceteris paribus).

questions.question_text: Suppose a researcher develops several MLR models. Model A has very low training error but substantially higher validation error. Model B has slightly higher training error but similarly low training and validation errors. Based on the module, which model should generally be preferred?

options.A: Model A, because the model with the lowest training error is always the best model.
options.B: Model A, because validation data should only be used after deployment.
options.C: Model B, because consistent performance across training and validation data suggests lower variance and better generalisation.
options.D: Model B only if its R² is exactly equal to Model A's R².

questions.explanation: Model A is overfitting to the training data (high variance on unseen data). Model B shows consistent and balanced error rates between training and validation data, indicating lower variance and better generalization ability.

questions.question_text: A multiple linear regression model has n = 55 observations, p = 2 independent variables, and: R² = 0.80. Which value is closest to the adjusted R²?
A multiple linear regression model is estimated using 55 observations and 4 independent variables. What are the degrees of freedom associated with SSR and SSE, respectively?

options.A: 4 and 50
options.B: 4 and 51
options.C: 54 and 50
options.D: 3 and 51

questions.explanation: For an MLR model with $n$ observations and $p$ independent variables: $df(SSR) = p = 4$, and $df(SSE) = n - p - 1 = 55 - 4 - 1 = 50$.

questions.question_text: An MLR model has the following F-test result: p-value = 0.018. The significance level is: α = 0.05. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Reject H₀ and conclude that all independent variables individually have significant relationships with y.
options.B: Fail to reject H₀ because the p-value is greater than zero.
options.C: Reject H₀ and conclude that there is statistically significant evidence that at least one of the regression coefficients β₁, …, βₚ is non-zero.
options.D: Reject H₀ and conclude that the intercept β₀ is statistically significant.

questions.explanation: The overall F-test tests $H_0: \beta_1 = \beta_2 = \dots = \beta_p = 0$ against $H_a$: at least one $\beta_j \neq 0$. Because $p$-value = 0.018 < $\alpha = 0.05$, we reject $H_0$ and conclude that at least one coefficient is significantly different from zero.

questions.question_text: Suppose an MLR model includes monthly income (x₁) and annual income (x₂) as independent variables. Their sample correlation coefficient is approximately 0.83. The overall F-test is statistically significant, but the individual t-test for monthly income has a p-value that is not statistically significant. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Monthly income has no relationship with monthly spending because its t-test is not significant.
options.B: The F-test must be incorrect because an individual variable has an insignificant t-test.
options.C: Due to the high correlation between monthly and annual income, monthly income may not provide significant additional explanatory value after annual income is already included in the model.
options.D: The insignificant t-test proves that the correlation between monthly and annual income is zero.

questions.explanation: Due to high multicollinearity between monthly and annual income ($r \approx 0.83$), the individual t-test tests the marginal contribution of monthly income given that annual income is already in the model. Monthly income provides redundant explanatory power.

questions.question_text: Suppose residual analysis from an MLR model reveals that the variance of the residuals appears to increase as the fitted values increase. Which regression assumption is most directly being questioned?

options.A: Homoscedasticity
options.C: Normality of ε
options.D: Independence of the independent variables

questions.explanation: Homoscedasticity assumes constant variance of the error terms across all fitted values $\hat{y}$. An increasing spread/variance violates this assumption (heteroscedasticity).

questions.question_text: Consider the following two observations about a multiple linear regression model: The residual plot against each individual Xᵢ appears approximately random. The residual plot against predicted values ŷ displays a pronounced U-shaped pattern. Which interpretation is most consistent with the material?

options.A: The model must be adequate because all individual Xᵢ residual plots are random.
options.B: The U-shaped pattern indicates that the constant variance assumption is violated, but the functional form is otherwise adequate.
options.C: The U-shaped pattern demonstrates that the independent variables are highly correlated.
options.D: The U-shaped pattern suggests that the assumed regression model may not adequately represent the relationship between the variables, despite the individual Xᵢ plots appearing acceptable.

questions.explanation: A curved (U-shaped) pattern in the residual plot against fitted values $\hat{y}$ indicates that the assumed linear regression model does not adequately capture the non-linear relationship between the variables, even if individual $X_i$ residual plots appear random.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes an outlier from an influential observation in multiple linear regression?

options.A: An outlier is always caused by an error in data collection, whereas an influential observation is always valid.
options.B: An outlier is a point that does not fit the trend of the remaining data, whereas an influential observation is one that can substantially affect the estimated regression equation if removed.
options.C: An outlier must have an extreme X-value, whereas an influential observation must have an extreme Y-value.
options.D: An outlier affects only the intercept, whereas an influential observation affects only the slope.

questions.explanation: An outlier is an observation with an unusually large residual that deviates from the overall pattern of the data. An influential observation is a data point whose presence or removal substantially alters the estimated regression parameters.

questions.question_text: A researcher identifies an influential observation in an MLR dataset. The observation substantially changes the estimated regression coefficients when it is removed. After investigation, the researcher confirms that: 1. The observation was recorded correctly. 2. It genuinely belongs to the population being studied. 3. It is not a data-entry or collection error. Which action is most appropriate according to the module?

options.A: Remove the observation because its strong influence makes the regression equation unreliable.
options.B: Retain the observation automatically and ignore its influence.
options.C: Examine the observation carefully and consider obtaining data on intermediate values of the independent variables to better understand the relationship between Xᵢ and Y.
options.D: Replace the observation with the predicted value ŷ so that it no longer influences the regression.

questions.explanation: When an influential observation is valid and correctly recorded, dropping it is improper. The researcher should investigate it carefully and collect additional observations at intermediate levels of the predictors to better understand the nature of the relationship.

questions.question_text: Two datasets have different means, but Dataset A has a coefficient of variation of 0.15 while Dataset B has a coefficient of variation of 0.55. What can be concluded?

options.A: Dataset A has a higher standard deviation in absolute terms
options.B: Dataset B shows greater relative variability compared to its mean
options.C: Both datasets have identical spread since standard deviation was not given
options.D: Coefficient of variation cannot be compared across different datasets

questions.explanation: The Coefficient of Variation ($CV = \frac{\sigma}{\mu}$) measures relative variability as a proportion of the mean. A higher $CV$ (0.55 vs 0.15) indicates that Dataset B exhibits greater dispersion relative to its average value.

questions.question_text: A simple linear regression of Y on a single independent variable X1 produces an R-Square of 0.25. When a second independent variable X2 is added to form a multiple regression, R-Square rises sharply to 0.78. What is the most likely explanation?

options.A: The sample size must have increased when X2 was added
options.B: R-Square increases only when the added variable is statistically significant and meaningfully improves the model
options.C: X1 alone was suffering from omitted variable bias, absorbing the effect of the excluded X2
options.D: The regression equation became nonlinear

questions.explanation: When an important explanatory variable ($X_2$) is omitted from a regression, the single predictor ($X_1$) suffers from omitted variable bias. Adding $X_2$ explains significant additional variation in $Y$, drastically increasing $R^2$ from 0.25 to 0.78.

questions.question_text: In a multiple regression's ANOVA table, MSR = 1200 and MSE = 40. What is the approximate F-statistic, and what does a very small associated p-value imply?

options.A: F = 30; we fail to reject the null hypothesis that all slope coefficients are zero
options.B: F = 30; we reject the null hypothesis that all slope coefficients are simultaneously zero
options.C: F = 0.033; the regression model is not significant
options.D: F cannot be computed without knowing the sample size

questions.explanation:
The overall model $F$-statistic is calculated as:
$$F = \frac{\text{MSR}}{\text{MSE}} = \frac{1200}{40} = 30$$
A very small $p$-value ($p < \alpha$) leads to rejecting $H_0: \beta_1 = \beta_2 = \dots = 0$, confirming the overall model is statistically significant.

questions.question_text: A regression model includes a binary (dummy) variable coded 1 for "Yes" and 0 for "No," with an estimated coefficient of 5.2 and a p-value close to zero. How should this coefficient be interpreted?

options.A: A one-unit increase in the dummy variable increases Y by 5.2%
options.B: The correlation between the dummy variable and Y is 5.2
options.C: The dummy variable explains 5.2% of the total variation in Y
options.D: On average, the "Yes" group has a Y value 5.2 units higher than the "No" group, holding other variables constant

questions.explanation: In dummy variable coding, the coefficient represents the estimated difference in the mean value of the dependent variable $Y$ between the indicator group ($X=1$, "Yes") and the reference baseline group ($X=0$, "No"), ceteris paribus.

questions.question_text: A correlation coefficient between two variables is calculated as 0.18, which seems weak. However, when a simple linear regression is run using these variables, the independent variable turns out to be statistically significant with a p-value near zero. What does this indicate?

options.A: A weak correlation does not automatically mean a variable lacks statistical significance in explaining part of the variability in Y
options.B: The correlation and regression results are contradictory, so one of them must be wrong
options.C: Statistical significance depends only on correlation strength
options.D: The R-Square value must be greater than 0.5 for any variable to be significant

questions.explanation: Statistical significance depends on both effect size and sample size ($n$). Even with a weak correlation ($r = 0.18$), a sufficiently large sample size can produce a very small standard error, proving the relationship is statistically non-zero ($p < 0.05$).

questions.question_text: While reviewing regression diagnostics, an analyst finds that most standardised residuals fall between -2 and +2, but a few are close to +3 or -3. What is the most appropriate conclusion?

options.A: The regression model is invalid and should be discarded immediately
options.B: Standardised residuals near ±3 always indicate a data-entry error
options.C: The model's R-Square must be recalculated because residuals are usually zero
options.D: A few observations may be unusual and should be investigated further, but they do not by themselves indicate that the model is invalid

questions.explanation: Standardized residuals are approximately standard normal; ~95% fall within $[-2, +2]$ and ~99.7% fall within $[-3, +3]$. Residuals near $\pm 3$ represent potential outliers that warrant investigation but do not automatically invalidate the entire model.

questions.question_text: In a multiple regression with three independent variables and 25 total observations, why is the Mean Square Error (MSE) calculated by dividing the Sum of Squares Error by 21 rather than 25?

options.A: Because only 21 of the observations were used in the regression
options.B: Because degrees of freedom are reduced by the number of estimated parameters, including the intercept
options.C: Because 4 observations were treated as outliers and removed
options.D: Because MSE is always calculated using n minus 4 by convention

questions.explanation: The degrees of freedom for error are calculated as $\text{DF}_{\text{error}} = n - p - 1$, where $n = 25$ and $p = 3$. This subtracts 4 total estimated parameters (3 slopes $\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3$ plus 1 intercept $\beta_0$), yielding $25 - 4 = 21$.

questions.question_text: A regression model's Adjusted R-Square is very close to its regular R-Square value across several model variations. What does this pattern generally suggest?

options.A: The independent variables being added are contributing genuine explanatory power rather than just inflating R-Square artificially
options.B: The model is definitely overfit and unreliable
options.C: Adjusted R-Square and R-Square are mathematically identical in all cases
options.D: The sample size must be very small for this to occur

questions.explanation: Adjusted $R^2$ penalizes the addition of non-informative predictors. If $R^2_{\text{adj}}$ remains very close to $R^2$, the predictors contribute sufficient explanatory power to overcome the degrees-of-freedom penalty.

questions.question_text: When examining a scatter plot of residuals against an independent variable, an analyst observes a clear curved pattern rather than a random scatter around zero. What does this most likely indicate?

options.A: The regression model has too many independent variables
options.B: The independent variable is statistically insignificant
options.C: The linear model may not adequately capture the true relationship between the variables
options.D: The standard error of the regression must be recalculated using a different formula

questions.explanation: A systematic curved pattern in a residual plot indicates a violation of the linearity assumption, suggesting that a non-linear or polynomial transformation (e.g., quadratic term) is required to capture the relationship.

questions.question_text: Two independent variables in a regression model are found to be highly correlated with each other, even though each appears significant when tested separately. What potential issue should the analyst be concerned about when interpreting the individual coefficients?

options.A: Omitted variable bias
options.B: Multicollinearity, which can make individual coefficient estimates unstable or difficult to interpret reliably
options.C: Heteroscedasticity in the residuals
options.D: A violation of the linearity assumption

questions.explanation: High correlation among independent variables creates multicollinearity. This inflates standard errors of the coefficients, making individual $t$-tests unreliable and parameter estimates sensitive to small data changes.
